blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: In this work, we propose Subspace Clifford Networks, a reformulation that replaces global cyclic rolling with grouped subspace interactions. Instead of sampling sparse cyclic diagonals across the entire $D$-dimensional channel space, we project the features into an aligned space $\R^{\tilde{D}} = \bigoplus_{g=1}^{G} V_g$ partitioned into $G$ low-dimensional groups $V_g \cong \R^k$ with $k \in \{2, 3, 4\}$. Within each $k$-dimensional group, we compute all $\binom{k}{2}$ wedge coordinates and concatenate them with $\operatorname{SiLU}$-activated coordinate-wise products, while sandwiching the grouped interaction between learnable $1\times 1$ linear projections to enable cross-group channel mixing. This design reduces intermediate feature expansion from $2|\mathcal{S}|D$ (typically $10D$ for 5 shifts) down to $1.5\tilde{D}$ ($k=2$), $2.0\tilde{D}$ ($k=3$), or $2.5\tilde{D}$ ($k=4$). Furthermore, exploiting the small, fixed group size $k \in \{2, 3, 4\}$, we implement a fused CUDA kernel that evaluates the forward interaction and a recomputation-based analytical backward pass using thread-local variables without allocating global-memory buffers for elementwise intermediates. Finally, we extend the backbone from an isotropic columnar layout to a multi-resolution Hierarchical Clifford Network with configurable per-stage subspace dimensions. Experiments on CIFAR-100 show that the proposed models substantially reduce parameter count and training time across both regimes, while the hierarchical variants also improve classification accuracy over the evaluated shift-based hierarchical baselines.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Modern computer vision backbones—ranging from Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) [ 1 , 2 ] to Vision Transformers (ViTs) [ 3 , 4 ] and State-Space Models (SSMs) [ 5 , 6 , 7 ] —commonly follow the “MetaFormer” design pattern [ 8 ] , interleaving spatial token mixers with channel-mixing Feed-Forward Networks (FFNs). Recently, CliffordNet [ 9 ] explored an alternative design based on Geometric Algebra (Clifford Algebra) [ 10 , 11 ] . By modeling feature evolution through the Clifford Geometric Product ( u ​ v = u ⋅ v + u ∧ v uv=u\cdot v+u\wedge v ), CliffordNet combines symmetric feature alignment (via an inner-product branch) and anti-symmetric structural variation (via an exterior wedge-product branch), achieving competitive accuracy without separate FFN blocks.

blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Clifford Algebra in Deep Learning. Geometric Algebra (Clifford Algebra) [ 10 , 11 ] provides a mathematical framework encompassing complex numbers, quaternions, and exterior algebra. Early Clifford neural networks [ 12 , 13 ] primarily targeted 3D physics simulations and PDE modeling with E ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{E}(3) -equivariance, parameterizing network weights as full multivectors (e.g., 2 4 = 16 2^{4}=16 components in 𝒞 ​ ℓ 4 , 0 \mathcal{C}\ell_{4,0} ). While expressive, multivector-valued weights increase matrix multiplication cost exponentially with algebra dimension. Recently, CliffordNet [ 9 ] applied a lightweight Clifford interaction over real-valued 2D vision feature maps, combining coordinate-wise inner products and shifted wedge differences without separate FFN blocks. Our work builds upon CliffordNet, replacing its cyclic shift approximation with grouped subspace interactions and a fused CUDA kernel.

blocks.en: Efficient Vision Backbones & Channel Mixing. Modern lightweight backbones achieve efficiency through structural priors. MobileNetV2 [ 1 ] employs inverted residuals with depthwise separable convolutions, while ShuffleNetV2 [ 2 ] introduces channel split and shuffle operations to facilitate cross-group information exchange. Vision Transformers [ 3 , 4 ] , modernized hierarchical ConvNets such as ConvNeXt [ 14 ] , and Vision SSMs [ 6 , 7 ] combine spatial token mixing with channel-mixing MLPs (typically using a 4 × 4\times channel expansion ratio). In contrast, our approach sandwiches low-dimensional ( k ∈ { 2 , 3 , 4 } k\in\{2,3,4\} ) subspace Clifford interactions—combining both coordinate-wise diagonal products and all ( k 2 ) \binom{k}{2} antisymmetric off-diagonal wedge terms—between 1 × 1 1\times 1 projections, maintaining a compact expansion ratio of 1.5 × 1.5\times to 2.5 × 2.5\times .

blocks.en: Reaction–Diffusion Motivation and Operator-Splitting Block Design. From a continuous dynamical perspective, feature evolution across both spatial neighborhoods and feature channels can be viewed as a coupled reaction–diffusion system : ∂ 𝐗 ∂ t = 𝒟 sp ​ ( 𝐗 ) + ℛ cli ​ ( 𝐗 ) \frac{\partial\mathbf{X}}{\partial t}=\mathcal{D}_{\text{sp}}(\mathbf{X})+\mathcal{R}_{\text{cli}}(\mathbf{X}) where 𝒟 sp ​ ( ⋅ ) \mathcal{D}_{\text{sp}}(\cdot) denotes a channel-wise spatial diffusion operator that propagates information across the 2D grid Ω \Omega , and ℛ cli ​ ( ⋅ ) \mathcal{R}_{\text{cli}}(\cdot) denotes a nonlinear cross-channel reaction operator driven by our subspace Clifford interaction. blocks.en: From Isotropic to Hierarchical Clifford Networks. While the original CliffordNet operates on an isotropic (single-resolution) grid, multi-scale feature hierarchies are beneficial for visual recognition. blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: In this section, we empirically evaluate our proposed Subspace Clifford Networks across both isotropic and multi-resolution hierarchical architectures. We design our experiments to examine four questions: 1. How does the grouped subspace Clifford interaction ( k ∈ { 2 , 3 , 4 } k\in\{2,3,4\} ) compare against shift-based rolling CliffordNet [ 9 ] in terms of classification accuracy, parameter count, and training time? 2. What is the effect of varying the subspace group size ( k = 2 , 3 , 4 k=2,3,4 ) and using stage-adaptive hybrid configurations in hierarchical backbones? 3. How much operator-level speedup and memory reduction does our fused CUDA kernel achieve compared to the native PyTorch implementation? 4. How does scaling the multi-resolution hierarchical backbone across depth affect accuracy and training cost?

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup

blocks.en: Dataset, Hardware, and Training Recipe. Following the evaluation protocol of CliffordNet [ 9 ] , we conduct benchmarks on the CIFAR-100 dataset (50,000 training images and 10,000 test images across 100 classes). All models are trained from scratch for 200 epochs using the AdamW optimizer with cosine learning rate decay, a weight decay of 0.1 0.1 , and standard data augmentation (AutoAugment and Random Erasing). No pre-trained weights or external data are used. All experiments and operator benchmarks are conducted on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU (24 GB GDDR6X VRAM).

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We introduced Subspace Clifford Networks, a reformulation of Clifford algebraic feature interactions that replaces global cyclic channel shifts ( torch.roll ) with grouped subspace interactions ( k ∈ { 2 , 3 , 4 } k\in\{2,3,4\} ) sandwiched between learnable 1 × 1 1\times 1 linear projections. Within each k k -dimensional group, the operator evaluates all ( k 2 ) \binom{k}{2} wedge coordinates together with k k SiLU \operatorname{SiLU} -activated coordinate-wise products, reducing intermediate channel expansion by up to 75 % 75\% compared to 5-shift rolling. Because the group size k k is small and fixed, we implemented a fused CUDA kernel with a recomputation-based backward pass that avoids intermediate elementwise buffers in device memory, achieving a 17.2 × 17.2\times operator speedup and a 50 % 50\% reduction in peak extra allocated memory on the evaluated k = 4 k=4 benchmark. Building on this module, we extended the backbone from single-resolution isotropic columns to multi-resolution Hierarchical Clifford Networks with configurable per-stage subspace dimensions. On CIFAR-100, our 12-layer hierarchical model reaches 80.25 % 80.25\% accuracy with 1.09 ​ M 1.09\text{M} parameters, and our 24-layer variant reaches 81.21 % 81.21\% accuracy while using fewer parameters than 12-layer shift-based baselines.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了子空间 Clifford Networks, Clifford代数特性相互作用的重构,它用分组子空间相互作用( k {{2, 3, 4} k\\\\ 2, 3, 4}) 取代了全局循环通道变换( hill.roll ) , 在可学习的 1 × 1 1\% 1 线性预测之间进行了三明治. 在每个 k - 维度组中, 操作员将所有 ( k 2)\ binom{ k}}\ binom{ k}} 楔形坐标与 k SiLU\ 操作器名称{ SiLU} - 激活的坐标导向产品一起评估, 将中间通道扩展减少 75% 75\\\\\ , 而5 班滚动 。 由于组大小kk是小而固定的,我们实施了一个带有重算基的CUDA内核,在设备内存中避免中间元素缓冲,实现17.2×17.2\时操作员加速,并在评估的k=4k=4基准上将峰值额外分配的内存减少50%50%. 在这个模块的基础上,我们扩展了主干线,从单分辨率异构列扩展到多分辨率的分层克里福德网络,每个阶段的子空间尺寸可配置. 在CIFAR-100上,我们的12层分级模型以1.09 M 1.09\text{M}参数达到80.25%的准确度,我们的24层变体达到81.21%的准确度,同时使用参数少于12层转向基准。
